The Navien NPE-180A2 is a condensing tankless water heater from Navien's NPE-2 series, with the ComfortFlow® recirculation pump and buffer tank built into the cabinet. No external pump, no dedicated return line hardware to buy separately.

Rated input is 10,000 - 150,000 BTU/h on natural gas or propane — the unit is certified for both. It modulates from 150,000 BTU/h all the way down to 10,000, so it is not running at full fire to fill a sink.

How much hot water you actually get

Navien rates every tankless unit by temperature rise, because the colder the incoming water, the less of it one burner can heat. Here is what the NPE-180A2 delivers:

Temperature rise Flow rate Typical use
35°F 8.4 GPM Warm-climate groundwater, or a preheated feed
45°F 6.5 GPM The usual design point across most of the U.S.
67°F 4.3 GPM Northern winter, incoming water near 40°F

Sized against a 2.5 GPM showerhead, the 67°F column is worth roughly one shower on the coldest day of the year, and more than that the rest of the year. Size to the 67°F row if your winter groundwater runs cold.

Minimum activation flow is 0.5 GPM, so it fires for a hand wash, not just a full shower.

With a Navien recirculation setup this unit also supports the low-flow activation option, down to under 0.01 GPM.

About ComfortFlow®: the pump and the buffer tank are inside the unit, not bolted on. That is what kills the cold-water sandwich when someone turns the shower off and back on, and it lets you run recirculation on a dedicated return line or on a crossover valve at the far fixture.

No sacrificial anode is required, there is a dedicated recirculation connection, and 2" rigid polyurethane foam insulation keeps standby heat loss under half a degree per hour. An indirect water heater is heated by a separate heat source, so before ordering confirm your boiler or other heat source can supply the required input, and check the drawings and submittal for connection locations and dimensions.

The VR8345M4302 is a gas control valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home) for universal appliances.

The gas valve is the component that admits fuel to the burner and shuts it off. It carries the main shutoff, the pressure regulator that holds manifold pressure steady as supply pressure varies, and the safety interlock that keeps gas off until the control system has proved it is safe to light.

This is a universal valve, built to serve intermittent pilot and direct ignition systems both. One part number covers applications that would otherwise take two, which is why it is the valve a service truck carries.

Gas appliance safety. A gas valve must match the appliance it is fitted to — ignition system, capacity, inlet pressure and gas type. Replacement is work for a licensed gas technician, and the appliance manufacturer's parts list is what decides the correct valve, not the physical fit of the threads. If the replacement does not match, the appliance can fail to light, fail to prove flame, or overfire.

The L4006H1004 is a control from Resideo (Honeywell Home) that senses boiler water temperature and switches the burner, the circulator, or both. It operates over a 100–240 °F range.

The aquastat is the control that keeps a hydronic boiler inside its working band. It holds the water hot enough to serve a call for heat and shuts the burner down before the boiler reaches a temperature the relief valve would have to handle.

This is a manual reset high limit. Once it trips, the control stays open until someone presses the button — the boiler does not simply restart when the water cools. That is deliberate: a high limit trip means something went wrong upstream, and a self-resetting limit would hide it.

This model ships without an immersion well. If you are replacing a control whose well is still sound, reuse it; if you are starting from a bare tapping, order a well to match.

A factory stop at 240 °F caps the adjustment so the high limit cannot be set past the point the boiler is rated for.

When you replace an aquastat, match the temperature range, the switch action and the differential to the control coming out, not to the boiler nameplate. A boiler will happily run on a control with the wrong range — it will simply cycle badly, or trip a limit that was never meant to be the working control.

The sensing bulb belongs in an immersion well, filled with heat conductive compound, threaded into the tapping the boiler manufacturer provided for it. A bulb strapped to the outside of a pipe reads the pipe, not the water, and it reads it late.

The F300E1001 is an electronic air cleaner from Honeywell Home, 16 in x 20 in.

An electronic air cleaner does not strain particles out of the air — it charges them and then collects them on plates of the opposite charge. That is a different physics from media filtration, and it shows up in the numbers: this unit holds back 81% of particles in the 0.3–1.0 micron range, where a MERV 11 media filter in the same cabinet size manages about a third of that. Small particles are the ones that reach deep into the lungs and the ones a pleated filter is worst at.

The trade is maintenance. The collecting cells are washable and they have to actually be washed — an electronic cleaner that goes a year without service stops collecting and becomes an expensive empty box. Plan on pulling the cells a few times a heating season.
